narrative.overview: This interface is a card catalogue you can flip through: entries on cool paper, one hairline per boundary, and a price tag that is the only warm thing on the page. It does not sell with decoration — it sells by being legible. The palette is deliberately cold: slate paper, white card stock, slate ink, and a single red reserved for money. Because there is no second warm hue anywhere, the price is impossible to miss without being loud. Dark mode is the same catalogue read under a lamp, with the same hairline logic and the same single red, lifted one step to stay readable on night paper.
keyCharacteristics: One accent family (red) used only for money and "pinned"; everything else is slate.
Flat at rest. No shadow, no gradient, no glow as decoration.
Two radius steps (8px controls, 12px containers) plus pills for chips and 4px badges.
System font stack; hierarchy built from weight and size, never from a second typeface.
Hairline borders separate everything; color fills are rare and always semantic.
Light and dark are the same design, one step apart in lightness.

rules.name: The One Warm Colour Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for money and for "pinned". If a red element is not a price, a pinned badge, or an error, it is a bug. Amber is its only sanctioned companion, and only on the high-value badge.

rules.name: The Ink-Is-The-Button Rule
rules.body: Primary actions fill with ink, never with a brand hue. There is no brand color to spend on a button — the catalogue authority comes from black type.

rules.name: The Two-Theme Rule
rules.body: Every color decision is made twice, from the same token names, in @theme and in html.dark. A raw Tailwind color name inside a component is a defect: it will not follow the theme.

rules.name: The No-Display-Type Rule
rules.body: There is no display face and no webfont. If a hierarchy problem seems to need a new typeface, it needs a weight or size change instead.

rules.name: The Four-Size Rule
rules.body: Any given screen uses at most four type sizes: 24, 18, 14, 12 (plus 10 only for badges). A fifth size means the hierarchy is being solved by accident.

rules.name: The Truncate-Once Rule
rules.body: Card names truncate in lists and wrap with break-words on detail pages. Detail headings, .prose bodies, and shop names must never overflow their column.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: No shadow, glow, or gradient at rest. If a surface needs to be distinguished, change its border or its tint, not its elevation.

rules.name: The Border-Or-Tint Rule
rules.body: Every "these are separate things" moment resolves to either a 1px hairline or one step of background tint. Never both, never a shadow.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: 8px for things you press, 12px for things that hold content. A 16px or 20px radius on a button or input is a defect.

rules.name: The Hairline-Always Rule
rules.body: Containers get a 1px border-border border. Removing it makes white cards disappear into the page in light mode.

dos: Do reach for `bg-surface` / `text-fg` / `border-border` / `bg-accent` before any raw Tailwind color. The token set is the theme switch.
Do verify every change in both themes at 320px and 1440px. Dark mode is a first-class state, not a filter.
Do keep interactive targets at least 24px tall (WCAG 2.5.8); pagination may shrink to 28px at 320px but never below.
Do put new content behind Directus. If the client would ever want to change a string or an image, it belongs in the CMS, not in a component.
Do keep filters, sort, and page in the URL so a filtered view can be shared and returns intact.
Do use `min-w-0` on grid and flex children that hold text; `break-words` alone does not reduce a min-content width.
Do give the three language versions the same structure and the same terminology, even where a translation would be shorter.
donts: Don't introduce a second warm color, a gradient, or a colored glow. Price-Tag Red and High-Value Amber are the entire permission.
Don't add a shadow at rest, or a radius outside the 8/12/16/4/full set.
Don't use `bg-white`, `text-slate-900`, or any raw palette name in a component — it will break dark mode.
Don't shrink text below 12px except the two 11px badges.
Don't use a de-emphasised colour for anything a user must read to understand why a container is empty — “暂无图片” is text, not decoration, and sits at the same value as Weak Text.
Don't let a fifth type size onto a screen to solve a hierarchy problem.
Don't hardcode client content (site name, shop details, announcement text, card copy) into components; the current values are placeholders and will be replaced.
Don't fabricate product imagery, testimonials, or review scores to fill a layout — the page must survive with “暂无图片” in every image well.
Don't reintroduce a cart, checkout, price comparison, or account surface. This is a catalogue, not a store.
